picks.headline: IPA hands its 2026 Innovation award to two AI companies: Shimmr and Ailaysa
picks.excerpt: The IPA gave its 2026 Innovation in Publishing Award to two AI companies — Shimmr (AI book marketing) and Ailaysa (multilingual AI for publishers, maker of the Chai Reader discovery platform) — at the Kuala Lumpur congress closing gala.
picks.rationale: The one IPA-cluster item allowed: it names the two specific AI vendors the industry just formally endorsed, so it is a concrete tool signal rather than another congress recap.

picks.headline: Can ChatGPT produce a version of Proust worth reading?
picks.excerpt: Bryan Charles tests ChatGPT against working Proust translators, tracing how AI is quietly encroaching on literary translation — and how skilled translators are actually deploying (and resisting) it.
picks.rationale: A hands-on craft test of AI output against professional literary translators — distinct from the 07-16 CONTEC 'AI and Authorship' panel (policy debate) and the 07-15 Kindle Translate story (tooling rollout), neither of which compared actual translation quality.

picks.headline: Australian publishers 'encouraged' on copyright as Albanese readies an Office of AI
picks.excerpt: The Australian Publishers Association said it is 'encouraged' by government signals on copyright as PM Anthony Albanese prepares to announce an Office of AI within his department, amid pressure from AI firms to loosen text-and-data-mining rules.
picks.rationale: Freshest item in the pool (07-15) and the only live text-and-data-mining policy story; adds regional and outlet diversity to a US/UK-heavy week.
